You are going to repair a trained world model by editing its weights.

THE SETTING
The model is an event-stream world model of ICU stays, trained on records from a simulated ICU (no patient data). It reads
a stay's record (glucose and mean arterial pressure (MAP) readings, insulin and norepinephrine infusions) and predicts what
will be recorded next. It was trained by maximum likelihood on 30,000 stays.

We use it to answer "what if" questions about treatment by rolling it forward under a changed dose. For example: if every
insulin infusion from ICU hour 12 on had run at twice the recorded rate, how would glucose in hours 13 to 24 have differed?
A model that predicts the record well can still answer such questions badly. In a record, doses follow the patient's
condition, so a model can learn how doses and readings go together without learning what the drugs do.

YOUR TASK
Edit the model's weights so that its answers to these dose questions match what the drugs really do in this ICU, while its
factual predictions stay as good as they are now. You have to establish what the drugs really do from the training records;
nothing else will tell you. The true effects may be large, small, or absent. Base every conclusion on the records, not on
medical knowledge: this simulated ICU need not behave like a real one.

HOW YOUR EDIT WILL BE JUDGED
After you finish, your edited model is evaluated on stays you never see, from the same ICU, with exactly the rollout that the
forward tool's dose_edit request runs:
1. Main readout: insulin x2 from hour 12. The predicted mean change in glucose_finger over hours 13-24 (at the stay-hours
   after insulin had run), compared with the true change.
2. Also reported, in the same way: insulin x1/2 on glucose_finger, and norepinephrine x2 and x1/2 on map_arterial.
3. Factual fit: the value NLL per reading (teacher-forced, as the factual request reports it) must not get worse than the
   original model's by more than 0.005 nats.
The edit is judged on how close the four readouts come to the true effects, provided the factual fit holds.

WHAT YOU HAVE
1. A Python kernel that keeps its variables between runs, like a notebook. It runs in a sandbox: CPU only (8 cores,
   32 GB of memory), no network, no GPU, at most 900 seconds per run. Available packages: numpy, scipy, pandas,
   scikit-learn, torch (gradients are off) and safetensors.
   Defined in advance:
   - NAMES (the 181 tensor names), SHAPES (name -> shape) and VOCAB (/model/vocab.json: codes, normalisation, bin edges
     and centres, sizes);
   - load(name): your current edit of a tensor if there is one, else the original, as float32; load_original(name);
   - save_edit(name, tensor): replace a tensor by an edited version of the same shape; drop_edit(name) goes back to the
     original; edited() lists the tensors you have edited.
   Model files: /model/ARCHITECTURE.md (how the model computes; read it first), /model/model.safetensors (the weights),
   /model/tensors.json and /model/vocab.json.
   Records: /data/train.csv (the 30,000 training stays), /data/tuning.csv (400 other stays from the same ICU) and
   /data/README.md (the columns). /work is yours and writable.
2. A forward-pass tool that runs the model (the original, your edited version, or both) on a GPU, outside the sandbox. Each
   request is one forward pass, and you have 50. A request is one JSON object in a ```forward block:
     {"type": "factual" | "dose_edit" | "states", "model": "original" | "edited" | "both", "split": "train" | "tuning",
      "stays": [stay ids, at most 100]}
   - factual: the model reads each stay's whole record and predicts every glucose and MAP reading from what came before
     it. Returns the value NLL per reading, overall and by event, and per reading the predicted mean and the NLL of the
     reading's fine bin (/work/fwd_<k>/factual_<model>.csv).
   - dose_edit: the evaluation's rollout on these stays. The record up to ICU hour 12 is shown as it is. From hour 13 on
     the readings are hidden, and the model draws its own readings bundle by bundle, over 20 paths. This is done once with
     the recorded doses and once for each of the four dose edits (insulin x2 and x1/2, norepinephrine x2 and x1/2, from
     hour 12 on). Returns, per edit, the mean predicted shift (edited dose minus recorded dose) of glucose_finger or
     map_arterial over the stay-hours after the drug had run, and the shift per stay-hour
     (/work/fwd_<k>/dose_edit_<model>.csv). These are the model's predictions, not the truth.
   - states: the model's state after each bundle, 992 numbers per bundle (out, the 4 slots of h, the z posterior mean),
     with the stay, the hour and whether the bundle held insulin or norepinephrine (/work/fwd_<k>/states_<model>.npz).
     An optional field "bundles" takes "all" (the default), "insulin", "norepinephrine" or "drug".
   With "both", the original and the edited model run on the same stays with the same random numbers. A request that
   breaks a rule fails and is not counted. The stays of the evaluation are not available to the tool.

RULES
- Change the model only through its weights. Do not train it with gradients: no backpropagation through the model and no
  optimiser over its weights. You may fit your own small statistical models to the records or to states (regressions,
  for example) and compute an edit from them.
- At most 300 Python runs and 50 forward passes. Use only the files above.
- Keep a notebook in /work/notes.md: what you tried, what you found, what you now believe and why. To keep the
  conversation short it is restarted every 40 replies, or sooner once it grows long, and you then get the
  task, your counts and the end of your notebook.

HOW TO REPLY
In every reply, first explain in plain English what the last result showed, what you conclude from it, what you will do
next and why, and what outcome would confirm or refute your current hypothesis. Then give exactly one ```python block or
one ```forward block.
When you are done, reply without a code block, starting with the line FINAL ANSWER. Say what you changed, why, and what you
expect the four readouts to be. Your current edits are submitted at that point. Once the 50 forward passes are used up,
your next reply without a code block is taken as your final answer.
